canon: THE canonical expansion/contraction numbers for this bundle — SKILL.md's expansion-budget row and i18n-check.py's NO_EXPANSION_ROOM advisory are both derived from this file. Edit here first, then re-derive both consumers.

regimes.shortString: UI microcopy — English source ≤ ~10 chars (labels, buttons, menu items, column headers). Expansion commonly +100–200% (factor ×2.0–×3.0); the shorter the source, the larger the factor.
regimes.runningText: Sentences and paragraphs — English source over ~70 chars. Expansion ~+30–50% for European languages (factor ×1.3–×1.5); CJK contracts.
regimes.note: One number cannot serve both regimes: a label budgeted with the running-text factor truncates its German translation, and a paragraph budgeted with the label factor wastes half the page. A card surface may declare `string_regime`; i18n-check.py defaults to runningText.

length_bands.comment: IBM's additional-space table for translation out of U.S. English (sources[1]); the W3C article (sources[0]) reproduces the same data as % of original.

sources.name: W3C Internationalization — 'Text size in translation' (Richard Ishida)
sources.grounds: length-band table as % of original (≤10 en chars → 200–300% of source); measured per-language ratios for the 5-char string 'views' (it ×3.0, de ×2.8, pt ×2.6, fr ×2.6, zh ×1.2, ko ×0.8); 'the smaller the source message, the higher the likely translation length'; CJK glyphs need ~2× Latin width; German compound nouns resist wrapping.

sources.name: IBM i Globalization — 'Text translation design for user interfaces'
sources.grounds: the additional-space-required table for text translated out of U.S. English: ≤10 chars +100–200% · 11–20 +80–100% · 21–30 +60–80% · 31–50 +40–60% · 51–70 +31–40% · >70 +30%.

default.notes: Use when the locale is not enumerated — mid-band of the cited tables.

de-DE.notes: W3C 'views' ×2.8. Compound nouns yield single long unwrappable words — min-content width matters as much as the factor.

fi-FI.notes: Agglutinative like German — long single words. Band-derived (no per-language citation).

ru-RU.notes: Same shape as German: sub-10-char strings commonly double or more ('Save' → 'Сохранить' ×2.25); running text ~+30–50%. The v1 single number ×1.2 was the running-text regime misread as the only regime.

ja-JP.notes: Character COUNT contracts but each glyph needs ~2× Latin width (W3C) — budget width, not characters; short strings can still exceed the English width.

zh-CN.notes: W3C 'views' ×1.2 width-adjusted ('次檢視'); running text contracts.

ko-KR.notes: W3C 'views' ×0.8 ('조회') — Korean can contract even on short strings; the ×1.0 short-string budget covers the labels that don't.

ar-EG.notes: Running text ~+20–25%; short strings spike like European locales. Band-derived.

he-IL.notes: Often near parity or shorter in running text; band-derived short-string headroom.

th-TH.notes: Band-derived; Thai stacks tone marks vertically — line-height, not just width (script-metrics.json).

hi-IN.notes: Band-derived; Devanagari conjuncts and matras raise vertical needs (script-metrics.json).
